native_result.HypoB: The effect of race on BA degree completion is the one that follows the described pattern: the White-vs-Black advantage is significant in the baseline social-background model (logit coefficient +0.5801, p=0.005, consistent in magnitude with 0.5024) but shrinks to roughly 0.04-0.12 and becomes statistically insignificant (p>0.6) once SES and academic characteristics (ASVAB ability composite and class percentile) are included (e.g., -0.1153, p=0.608 without family size; -0.0378, p=0.861 with SES+percentile), i.e., the racial gap in BA completion is accounted for by SES and academic preparation.
